hero.h1: Understanding Down Payment Assistance Programs in Florida
hero.lead: Dive in to uncover how Florida's diverse down payment assistance programs can catapult your dream of homeownership from mere aspiration to exciting reality!

h1: Understanding Down Payment Assistance Programs in Florida
sections:
Are you a First Time Homebuyer looking to buy a home?

Embarking on the journey of homeownership is exciting, but the financial intricacies can sometimes feel overwhelming. Luckily, there are organizations like Hometown Lenders, that aim to simplify the process and help you navigate your way to your first home. A trusted mortgage brokerage firm, Hometown Lenders, leverages top-notch technology and unparalleled customer service to guide you through your mortgage process seamlessly. Our primary focus has always been you, the customer, and we’re committed to doing business the right way. Now, let’s delve into a comprehensive look at down payment assistance programs in the state of Florida, which could provide a significant financial boost to your home buying journey.

The Florida Assist Bond

The Florida Assist Bond offers a second mortgage, the FL Assist, which provides $10,000 for all loans. This loan is non-amortizing and deferred, meaning it carries no monthly payment. However, it’s important to note that repayment isn’t forgivable and will become due when the property is sold, transferred, refinanced, or if the mortgagor stops living in the property. The Florida Assist can’t be combined with other FL Housing’s down payment assistance programs.

Bond First Mortgage Options

Florida Housing provides a couple of first mortgage options for eligible first-time home buyers. The first is the Florida First (FL First), a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage for FHA and USDA-RD loans, with the rate determined by FL Housing. There’s also the FL HFA Preferred, which offers eligible borrowers a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage and reduced mortgage insurance premiums for borrowers with income at or below 80% of AMI.

Understanding the Veterans Exception

Veterans, who’ve served in active military, naval, or air service and honorably discharged, aren’t required to be first-time home buyers to qualify for these programs. To qualify under the Veterans Exception, borrowers must certify that they meet the requirements on the Mortgagor Affidavit and provide a valid DD214.

Exploring The Florida Homeownership Loan Program 

The Florida Homeownership Loan Program Second Mortgage (FL HLP) offers $10,000 as a fully-amortizing, second mortgage with a 15-year term. This loan carries a monthly payment, but similar to the Florida Assist, the unpaid balance becomes payable in full under certain conditions such as sale, transfer, or refinancing of the property.

Taking Advantage of Forgivable Second Mortgage Option

Florida Housing also provides a forgivable second mortgage option, which offers assistance calculated as a percentage (3%, 4% or 5%) of the total loan amount. This five-year, deferred loan carries no monthly payment and is forgiven at a rate of 20% per year on the anniversary of loan closing, over the term of the second mortgage loan.

Spotlight on Florida Hometown Heroes 

The FL Hometown Heroes program presents additional benefits, such as lower first mortgage rates, and a generous down payment and closing cost assistance. It offers a 5% second mortgage – 5% of the total loan amount capped at $35,000 – in down payment and closing cost assistance as a 0%, non-amortizing, 30-year, repayable second mortgage.

Exploring Hometown Heroes First Mortgage Options

Florida Housing offers government and conventional loan options to eligible participants in the Florida Hometown Heroes Loan Program. These options include the Florida First Heroes, the HFA Preferred Heroes, and the FL HFA Advantage Heroes – all designed to aid borrowers with affordable, 30-year, fixed-rate mortgages and automatic qualification for down payment assistance.

Common Questions About Florida Down Payment Assistance for First-time Buyers

What is the biggest negative when using down payment assistance?

The biggest negative when using down payment assistance is that it often involves a higher interest rate or additional fees on your FHA loan or first mortgage loan, effectively increasing the long-term cost of your home. Also, some programs may require you to repay the assistance if you sell the house before a certain period.

Who qualifies for down payment assistance in Florida?

To qualify for down payment assistance in Florida, you must be a first-time homebuyer or a qualified veteran, meet certain income and credit score requirements, and plan to use the purchased property as your primary residence. Housing finance agencies and mortgage lenders may have additional requirements as per federal housing and urban development guidelines.

What is the down payment assistance for 580 credit score in Florida?

In Florida, if you have a credit score of 580, you may qualify for the FHA mortgage program, which allows for lower down payments and can be combined with certain down payment assistance programs. However, the specific amount of down payment assistance will depend on your individual circumstances, such as income, loan amount, and the particular program rules.

What is the income limit for down payment assistance in Florida?

The income limit for down payment assistance in Florida can vary based on the program and the location of the home. Some programs may have county-specific income limits or be designed to serve low-to-moderate-income households. Always check with your mortgage lender or housing finance agency for precise information.

Which government program requires the least down payment?

The government program that requires the least down payment is the USDA Rural Development loan program, which allows for 100% financing in eligible rural areas. The VA loan program for veterans also allows for zero down payment. The FHA mortgage program, while it requires a down payment, the minimum is quite low at 3.5% for those with a credit score of 580 or higher.

Wrapping Up The Down Payment Assistance, First-time Homebuyer Program Talk

In conclusion, Florida offers a broad range of down payment assistance programs designed to help aspiring homeowners turn their dreams into reality. From the Florida Assist Bond to the Florida Homeownership Loan Program and the special provisions for our Hometown Heroes, there are numerous options that cater to diverse needs. Each program has unique advantages and is structured to ensure that homeownership is more accessible, affordable, and sustainable. While the home buying process can be complex, organizations like Hometown Lenders, are committed to simplifying the process and providing crucial support every step of the way. Navigating these programs successfully could provide significant financial relief and accelerate your journey to homeownership.

h1: Understanding Lot and Land Loans: A Comprehensive Guide
sections:
Are you dreaming of building your own custom home, nestled on a picturesque piece of land? Perhaps you’ve found the perfect lot to build your dream home, but you’re not quite sure how to finance it. This is where lot and land loans come into play, and Luminate Bank is here to shed light on this topic. In this comprehensive guide, we’ll walk you through what land and lot loans are, how they work, and how they can help you turn your dream property into a reality.

What Are Lot and Land Loans?

Land and lot loans are specialized types of loans that are designed to help individuals purchase vacant land or lots for future development or investment. These loans are different from traditional mortgages used to buy an existing home. Instead, they are tailored to the unique needs and challenges of buying undeveloped land.

Key Features of a Land Loan:

  1. Shorter Loan Terms: Land and lot loans typically have shorter terms than traditional mortgages. These terms can range from 3 to 10 years, with some lenders offering longer options.
  2. Higher Interest Rates: Interest rates for land and lot loans are often higher than those for traditional mortgages. This is because lenders perceive them as riskier since there is no existing structure on the property.
  3. Down Payment Requirement: Lenders typically require a larger down payment to get a land loan, often in the range of 25% to 50% of the property’s purchase price.
  4. Limited Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio: The LTV ratio is the percentage of the property’s value that the loan covers. Land and lot loans typically have lower LTV ratios, usually capped at around 70% to 80%.
  5. Balloon Payments: Many loan options feature balloon payments, which means that the remaining balance of the loan is due at the end of the term. Borrowers often need to refinance or pay off the loan by selling the land or obtaining a construction loan before the balloon payment comes due.

How Do Land Loans Work?

Understanding how loans for land purchase work is essential before embarking on your land purchase journey. Here’s a step-by-step breakdown of the process:

  1. Determine Your Budget: Before you start looking for land for your dream home, establish your budget. Consider not only the purchase price of the raw land but also additional costs like property taxes, insurance, and potential site preparation expenses.
  2. Research Properties: Begin your search for the perfect type of land. Consider factors such as location, size, zoning regulations, and access to utilities. It’s crucial to find a property that aligns with your long-term goals.
  3. Prequalify with a Lender: Contact a reputable lender like Luminate Bank to get prequalified for a lot or land loan. They will assess your financial situation, credit score, and provide you with an estimate of the loan amount you can secure.
  4. Property Appraisal: Once you’ve chosen a property, the lender will typically require an appraisal to determine its current market value. This appraisal helps determine the loan amount and interest rate.
  5. Loan Approval: If the property passes the appraisal and you meet the lender’s criteria, your land or lot loan will be approved. At this point, you’ll also finalize the loan rates and terms, including the interest rate and repayment schedule.
  6. Down Payment: Most loans require a down payment as stipulated by the lender. This is a significant upfront cost, so be sure to have your finances in order.
  7. Loan Repayment: Make regular payments as per the agreed-upon schedule. Some borrowers may choose to pay off the loan in full or refinance it into a construction loan for the land and start building.
  8. Future Development: Once you buy land or a lot, you can move forward with your plans, whether that’s to build a house or holding the property for future investment.

Benefits of Land and Lot  Mortgage Loans

Land and lot loans can offer several benefits to prospective buyers:

  1. Land Preservation: Securing a plot of land allows you to preserve the land and protect it from potential development by others.
  2. Customization: You have the freedom to design and build your dream home to your specifications on the purchased land.
  3. Investment Potential: Undeveloped land can appreciate in value over time, making it a potentially profitable investment.
  4. Strategic Timing: You can buy the land now and build when the timing is right, whether that’s immediately or in the future.

h1: Is a Reverse Mortgage Right for You?
sections:
The Easiest Way to Get the Most Out of a Reverse Mortgage

For those who are 55 years of age or older, a reverse mortgage is an excellent vehicle for tapping into the equity of your home. Whether you’re looking to simply get some extra income, cover healthcare costs, or anything else, a reverse mortgage might be right for you.

At Southern Home Loans, we make applying for a reverse mortgage as easy as 1, 2, 3. Our experience works for you to answer all your questions on this type of mortgage, whether it will work for you and, if it is, get the best possible rates.

What is a reverse mortgage?

A reverse mortgage is the opposite of a regular mortgage. When you have a regular mortgage on your home, you make payments on your home every month to the bank or lender. With a reverse mortgage, you are actually the one who gets paid.

Part of the equity on your home is taken and given to you in payments. It’s a payment in advance on your home’s equity.

So long as you continue living in your home, you won’t have to make any payments on your reverse mortgage.

Why is a reverse mortgage beneficial?

As you get older, you’re likely going to have unplanned expenses that you’ll need to cover. You might be a good candidate for a reverse mortgage if:

  • You have medical costs that you’re struggling to afford
  • You need help paying off your existing regular mortgage
  • You want to supplement your income
  • You want to perform remodels or additions to your home

A reverse mortgage can be greatly beneficial for retirees who need a little extra help to get by, as it increases their income without any immediate principle or interest payments. Our specialists can help you determine if a reverse mortgage is right for you.

Are there any downsides to a reverse mortgage?

While you won’t have to make payments on the principle or interest for as long as you’re living in your home, you will have to pay utilities, real estate taxes, and flood and hazard insurance premiums.

More importantly, however, is the fact that a reverse mortgage can use up your home’s equity. If you are planning to leave your home to your spouse or heirs, then you might consider a different type of loan, because the loan and the interest will have to be repaid before the estate is settled.

However, if there is still equity left in the home after the repayment, it will be transferred to heirs and debt won’t be transferred to heirs or the estate.

How we can help

Our experts can go over your home’s equity with you in order to help you determine whether a reverse mortgage is right for you. We’ll go over the pros and cons with you and make sure to provide you with the best option.

We also have the fastest, easiest approval process available, which means we handle all the complicated aspects so you don’t have to worry about them.

h1: Affordable Homeownership for Marion County & Ocala Buyers
sections:
SHIP Purchase Assistance Program

The SHIP (State Housing Initiatives Partnership) Purchase Assistance Program helps qualified buyers in Marion County and the City of Ocala secure down payment and closing cost assistance, making homeownership more affordable and within reach.

At Southern Home Loans, we guide you through the entire process from pre-approval to closing. We know the program guidelines inside and out, and we make it simple.

What Is the SHIP Program?

The SHIP Purchase Assistance Program provides down payment and closing cost assistance to income-qualified buyers purchasing a primary residence in Marion County or the City of Ocala.

Funds are provided through:

  • State Housing Incentive Program (SHIP) funds
  • Federal HUD HOME funds

This program is designed to remove one of the biggest barriers to buying a home: upfront cash.

How Much Assistance Is Available?

The amount of assistance is based on household income (Area Median Income – AMI):

Income must fall below 140% of the area median income as determined annually by HUD/FHFC. We’ll help you determine where you fall and what that means for your buying power.

Who Is Eligible?

To qualify for SHIP assistance, buyers must meet several requirements.

Homeownership Status

  • You cannot currently own a home

Residency

  • Must have been a Florida resident for at least 1 year
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or documented permanent resident (minimum 2 years with tax returns)

Credit Requirements

  • Minimum 580 credit score
  • One year of satisfactory credit
  • Bankruptcies must be discharged for 2 years (3 if a home was included)
  • Foreclosure, short sale, or deed in lieu must be completed for at least 3 years

Outstanding unpaid judgments or collections must be resolved or on a documented repayment plan.

Employment

  • Two years of employment history (including part-time)
  • Self-employed borrowers must show 2 years of tax returns with Schedule C

What Type of Loans Are Allowed?

SHIP assistance can be paired with: Conventional, FHA, VA, and USDA loans.

Loan terms must be:

  • 30-year fixed (38 years for USDA)
  • Fixed rate
  • No balloon, ARM, prepayment penalty, demand feature, or negative amortization

We’ll structure your financing to ensure it meets program guidelines.

Why Work With Southern Home Loans and Luminate Bank?

Programs like SHIP have strict guidelines and timelines. One missed detail can delay closing.

That’s where we come in. We can:

  • Structure your loan to meet SHIP requirements
  • Coordinate directly with Community Services
  • Ensure your pre-approval letter meets all program standards
  • Help you stay on track through inspections, disclosures, and funding
  • Make sure there are no surprises at closing

We handle the complexity so you can focus on finding the right home.

If you’re looking to buy in Marion County or Ocala and need help with down payment and closing costs, this program could be the opportunity you’ve been waiting for.

Let’s run the numbers.

sections:

If you’re a low or middle-income individual or family in a rural area, we can help you get qualified for a USDA Loan to buy or repair a home in a rural area.

There are often different terms and interest rates for the USDA loan process, which is why applying with Southern Home Loans is your best bet. Because we provide so many different options to all our customers, you don’t have to worry about missing the best possible loan.

Why would a USDA Loan be right for you?

  • You’re looking to purchase a home in a rural area
  • You’re looking to repair or renovate a home in a rural area
  • You receive a low or middle income and want to qualify for a home loan

What are the different types of USDA Loans?

USDA Loans come in many different forms. Here are a few that you might be interested in:

  • Single-family guaranteed homeownership loan
  • Single-family direct homeownership loan
  • Rural repair and rehabilitation loan
  • Mutual self-help loan

Why choose Southern Home Loans for your USDA Loan?

Because there are so many different types of USDA Loans, you need to make sure that you’re applying for the one that fits your specific situation the best. With so much experience on our side, we’ve been able to help families of all types qualify for the most fitting USDA Loan.

Over the years, we’ve found that the best way to give our customers the loan that fits their needs the best is by showing them everything they qualify for. This allows them to pick and choose their preferred loan based upon their individual circumstances.

With a simple and personalized approach, it’s incredibly easy to find the loan that meets every one of your needs while also giving you the best interest rates possible.

h1: VA Loans that serve for those who served!
sections:
Advantages of a VA Loan

If you’re a United States military Veteran, then it’s always a good idea to take advantage of a VA home loan. This is a loan that the United States Department of Veterans Affairs guarantees, and it’s provided by lenders who are qualified.

We want to save you money on your monthly payments and interest rates, and we’ve established a system that has proven to do just that. Southern Home Loans is fully qualified to offer VA Loans to military Veterans, and we make the entire process as easy as possible. We can provide long-term home financing to Veterans and their spouses.

Why and how do we make VA Mortgages simple?

At Southern Home Loans, we care deeply about those who have served our country. We understand the sacrifice that our veterans and their families have made, and we want to ensure that they never have any trouble securing their home loans.

We’ve been in this business for a long time, and we’ve set up the tools needed to make your application for your VA loan easy. Simply fill out the quick VA Loan Qualifier for free and be on your way to owning your home!

What are the benefits of VA Loans?

The mortgage doesn’t always require a down payment

Available to all Veterans and active members of the military

No need for mortgage insurance

Our commitment to serving those who served

Because we appreciate the sacrifices our vets and their families have made, and we know the difficulties that they sometimes face, we strive to make it easy for them to get into their homes with the best home loans possible.

You can apply online and qualify for your VA loan right here on our site, which makes everything quicker and easier for you. You never have to hassle with trying to figure out which loan is best, as we give you all your options in one place to make the decision easy.

Homes to Heroes

Save even more with the Homes to Heroes program.

hero.h1: The Mortgage Process
hero.lead: Greetings! I’m excited about the opportunity to assist you and your family with your new home. I wanted to take a moment and introduce myself and my team. I have been in the world of Real Estate as a Mortgage loan officer for many years. My team will make this experience smooth and seamless. Thank you for the opportunity to earn your business. We know you have many options when it comes to lending and we will make sure this is a red carpet experience for you. Sincerely,

h1: The Mortgage Process
sections:
Loan Checklist

Thank you for considering us as your mortgage lender! Below is a typical document list for the mortgage process. You can upload these to your Simple Nexus portal. After our review, we might request additional documents. Submitting these documents doesn't obligate you to accept our mortgage terms or require them for a Loan Estimate.Apply Now

All Borrowers

  • Copy of unexpired picture identification (e.g., Driver’s License, VISA, Passport, Military ID, or State Issued ID) for each applicant
  • Most recent two (2) months of bank statements, ALL numbered pages
  • Most recent two (2) months of brokerage statements, ALL numbered pages
  • Most recent two (2) months of retirement statements, ALL numbered pages
  • Terms of withdrawal for retirement accounts
  • Executed Purchase Contract/Agreement with all addendums
  • Supporting documentation for any recent deposits not noted as automated payroll deposits
  • Homeowners insurance policy if refinancing or information for the new property – agent and company name with phone number
  • If any deposits or funds for closing are from a Gift (e.g., from relative, employer, non-profit, etc.), then more documentation will be required depending on the loan program – check with your Loan Officer for a specific list for your chosen program
  • Copy of Earnest Money Check (a copy of the cleared check may be required as well, check with your Loan Officer)
  • Copy of Social Security card

Self-employed Borrowers

*Own at least 25% of a business, corporation, and/or partnership
  • Most recent 30 days of pay stubs for each income source for each applicant
  • W-2, K-1, and/or 1099 forms for the previous two (2) years for each applicant
  • Most recent two (2) years of personal federal income tax returns with ALL schedules for each applicant, if filed separately

Salaried Borrowers

  • Most recent two (2) years of business federal income tax returns with ALL schedules for each applicant, if applicable
  • Year-To-Date Profit/Loss Statement and Balance Sheet for any sole proprietor company, partnership, or corporation in which you have 25%or more ownership
  • W-2, K-1, and/or 1099 forms for the previous two (2) years for each applicant
*All rates and terms subject to change at anytime without notice. This is not a commitment to lend.

What to Expect
Between Now and Closing

First 30 Business Days After ContractPrequalify for your loan now →

Loan Structuring Call - Virtual meeting using Zoom/Teams to set up your loan options and address any questions and concerns. Your Loan Officer will send out your prequalification letter and Loan Estimate list after the call.

Disclosures - Receive your initial set of disclosures (Non-binding and required for file setup)

Loan Documents - Send your initial needs list back to us via email. The team will request any additional documents that may be needed.

Setup/Processing/Underwriting - The team will review your documents and move your loan forward to set up then processing, then underwriting for your initial underwriting review

Once you have your loan conditionally approved, your interim wait time will begin. The file will be on hold till approximately 60 days until closing. If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to the team.

30-60 Days Prior to Closing

Documentation Update - During this time, the Southern Home Loans will update your file for closing. The first thing we will do is refresh your credit report. After that, your processor will check if the documents that we have on file (paystubs, etc.) are the most current and if your file is complete. Any items that your processor requests from you are highly time
sensitive.

10-45 Days Prior to closing

Locking your rate - Please reach out to your loan officer at this time to lock in your interest rate. Within three days of locking your rate, you will receive a DocuSign disclosure bundle with your updated estimated terms from our team. It is very important that you DocuSign the bundle in a timely manner. Please reach out to one of our team members with any questions. We’re happy to help!

Underwriting Re-review - The underwriter will review your new documents and information and advise if any additional clarification or documentation is needed for final approval (if so, your processor will promptly reach out to you).

Insurance - We will verify your insurance information with the insurance provider you have selected for homeowners insurance. It is very important that you provide the Southern Home Loans with the name and contact information of your homeowners insurance provider 30 days in advance, no later than 20 days prior to closing to prevent delays.

5-10 Days Prior to Closing

Final Required Third Party Verifications - Around this time, we will conduct required audits and verifications that must be completed within 10 days of your closing date. It is very important that you do not change your employment information or marital status, or apply for any new lines of credit during the loan process.

Closing Preparations - Our closing department will begin preparing your documents for closing. During this time, we will connect with the title company and other third parties to finalize our figures.

Underwriting Final Approval Submission - Upon receipt of the final required third party verifications, your loan will be resubmitted to underwriting for final approval.

Appraisal - Your appraisal will be received for your new home, and we will send you a copy for your records upon receipt. If you do not receive a copy of your appraisal at least prior to closing, please contact a member of our team.

3-5 Days Prior to Closing

Closing Disclosure: Once all your figures are confirmed with the title company, builder, insurance provider, etc., you will receive a closing disclosure from our closing department via DocuSign. This document will contain the final amount you will need to bring in a cashier’s check payable to the title company. It is very important that you sign this final closing disclosure immediately upon receipt on the same day. It is time stamped and we are held to very strict guidelines by the federal government. Failure to do so could delay your closing.

Day of Closing

Closing: You will have received closing instructions (date, time, address, etc.) by this time. We recommend that you print these instructions. On the day of closing, bring your cashier’s check payable to the title company, your driver’s license, and your spouse if he/she is not on the loan with you to your appointment. Because Texas is a community property state, your other half must also be at the closing.

Congratulations in Advance!hello world!

The DOs & DON'Ts of Financing a Home

Talk to us today and learn how we can help you! Don't make common mistakes, contact our team if you think any of the DON'Ts are unavoidable. We can help determine what to do so your loan is least negatively affected.Apply Now

The DOs

  • Call if you have questions or concerns
  • Tell your friends and family about the Southern Home Loans
  • Get a goods night sleep; you were referred to our team for a reason and can rely on us for red carpet service

The DON'Ts

  • Change jobs, quit your job or become self-employed
  • Buy or trade a vehicle
  • Increase debt/balances or miss a payment
  • Spend money you have set aside for closing
  • Buy furniture or appliances or make a new credit application
  • Originate credit inquiries (no new loans, credit cards or lines of credit)
  • Make large deposits or transfer funds
  • Change bank accounts
  • Co-sign any loan

h1: Mortgages for Military Members: A Look at VA Loan Requirements
body:
Buying a home requires significant planning and preparation. At the same time, it can also be a very exciting and rewarding experience that you deserve to enjoy. 

Mortgages are a major financial commitment and can often be daunting to understand. Many veterans, however, have access to special home loan benefits through the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) that can make financing easier and more affordable. 

Knowing the ins and outs of VA loan requirements can bring you peace of mind during this homebuying process. Consider this statistic about approved VA mortgages. Already in the first quarter of 2023, over 104,000 loans have been approved by the VA. 

The good news is that below is the comprehensive guide you need in order to get started. Keep reading to learn how to optimize your chance of getting a VA mortgage. 

The Basics of VA Benefits

The United States provides a variety of benefits to its veterans. Statistics show that as of 2021, there were around 16.5 million veterans living in the United States. If you’re in the number, you may be eligible for benefits and assistance such as a VA-specific mortgage loan.

Benefits include providing educational assistance, vocational rehabilitation programs, and more. In particular, there are home loan guaranty programs. These provide loans to purchase a home with low-interest rates and no down payments required for qualified applicants.

If you have any questions about VA programs or how they could help you or someone you know, it’s best to contact a local VA office directly. They can answer any questions you may have about eligibility requirements and other details that may apply. It might be a useful step to take before you even start applying for a VA mortgage.

The Basics of VA Loan Requirements for a Mortgage

Knowing what requirements you need to meet for a VA mortgage loan is an important step in achieving homeownership. (Remember, if this process seems too daunting, you can still reach out to industry experts to assist you along the way.)

It’s important to note that the VA doesn’t provide loans directly. Instead, it guarantees the loans of lenders who approve them. To be eligible for a VA loan, you must meet at least one of the following criteria:

  1. You served 181 days during peacetime
  2. You served 90 days during wartime
  3. You have six years of service in the National Guard or Reserve
  4. You are a surviving spouse of a veteran who died in service or as a result of service-related disabilities

Just because you qualify according to one of those four requirements, though, doesn’t mean you automatically get a new home. It’s important to stay organized during the entire home-buying process.

For one thing, you’ll need the proper identification and documentation to prove your eligibility. Take the time to gather these materials together. Keeping good records and copies of those records can make the rest of the application process continue smoothly. 

Types of VA Mortgage Loans

There are several types of VA mortgage loans available depending on your needs and circumstances. The most common type is the traditional 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. This one offers fixed monthly payments over the life of the loan and requires little to no down payment (for approved veterans, of course, there would be no down payment at all).

A traditional fixed-rate mortgage is ideal for those who plan on staying in their home long-term. If you want to avoid any potential interest rate increases over time, consider applying for this VA loan.

There are also 15-year fixed mortgage rates. That would mean you’d be able to pay off the entire home much more quickly. At the same time, remember that those monthly payments would be higher.

Another option is called an adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM). This version offers lower initial rates but can increase after an introductory period. 

Refinancing Your Home as a Veteran

The VA also offers Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loans (IRRRLs). These allow veterans with existing VA loans to refinance into lower interest rates without having to go through an extensive underwriting process again.

Additionally, some lenders offer special programs such as cash-out refinances. These could let veterans withdraw equity from their homes for debt consolidation, home improvements, college tuition costs, etc.

Perhaps you’d be interested in making energy-efficient upgrades to your home. You know that it would increase the property’s overall value and reduce utility bills over time. Well, the VA’s energy-efficient refinanced mortgage might be what you’re looking for. 

What to Do After Your Mortgage Loan Is Approved

Once you’ve been approved for your VA mortgage, you can start with the fun of searching for a new home. There are great online options to research potential new homes in the neighborhoods you find interesting. Of course, you can always rely on an in-person real estate agent, too. 

It’s also worth noting how important it is to keep your finances in mind every step of the way, even after you get approved for a mortgage loan. Think about the costs of decorating and buying furniture, for instance. You’ll want to ensure you’ve set aside plenty of money for those other upfront costs.

Don’t Be Afraid to Ask Industry Experts for Help

Understanding all of the details involved in securing a VA mortgage can seem overwhelming at first glance. You don’t have to go through this process alone, though. 

Not only could your local VA office assist you in your application process for a mortgage loan. In addition, don’t be afraid to talk with mortgage lenders about their expertise. They might have some tips and tricks that could make the purchasing process even smoother. 

Start Applying for Your VA Loan Today

Once you’ve met the VA loan requirements and are now a potential homeowner, congratulations! This is an exciting part of life, and we’d love to be there right alongside you. 

That’s why we hope you work with us when looking for your ideal mortgage loan. Take some time to learn more about VA loans and how to get approved for them at your convenience.

hero.h1: Things To Do In Marion County, FL & Economic Status
hero.lead: Welcome to Marion County, Florida – a dynamic blend of economic vitality and natural beauty. With a population of 396,415 and a median household income of $55,265, this county offers a thriving job market, a rich cultural scene, and outdoor wonders. Let’s explore what makes Marion County, Florida, special.

h1: Things To Do In Marion County, FL & Economic Status
sections:

Employment:

Median home price:

Things to do in Marion County, FL

Marion County, Florida, offers a diverse range of activities and experiences for everyone. Here are some ideas for things you can do, categorized by interest:

Outdoor Activities:

Explore natural wonders:

  • Visit Silver Springs State Park and take a glass-bottom boat tour over crystal-clear springs.
  • Hike or bike the Santos – Belleview Trail, offering scenic views and wildlife encounters.
  • Go swimming, kayaking, or canoeing in the numerous springs and rivers, including Rainbow Springs State Park and Juniper Springs.
  • Climb the Ocala National Forest for stunning panoramic views.

Experience the horse capital of the world:

  • Take a horseback riding tour through the scenic landscapes of Ocala.
  • Visit the renowned World Equestrian Center for world-class horse shows and events.
  • Learn about the history and culture of horses at the Appleton Museum of Art’s “The Horse in Art” exhibit.

Enjoy family-friendly fun:

  • Cool off at one of the many splash pads, including Wilma Loar Splash Park in Belleview and Lily’s Splash Pad in Ocala.
  • Visit the Discovery Center of Ocala for interactive exhibits on science, technology, and the environment.
  • Go bowling at Bowlero East Ocala or spend a day at Laser Tactics for laser tag fun.
  • Zip Lining

Cultural and Historical Activities:

Delve into history:

  • Explore the Ocala Downtown Square, featuring historic buildings, shops, and restaurants.
  • Visit the Fort King National Historic Landmark, a replica of a British fort from the 18th century.
  • Take a walking tour of Ocala and learn about its fascinating history and architecture.

Immerse yourself in art and culture:

  • Stroll through the beautiful Tuscawilla Art Park and discover sculptures, murals, and other works of art.
  • Catch a performance at the historic Marion Theatre or the Ocala Civic Theatre.
  • Explore the Appleton Museum of Art for a diverse collection of art and artifacts.

Unique Experiences:

Go on a thrilling airboat tour:

  • Experience the excitement of gliding across the water and encounter alligators, birds, and other wildlife.
  • Several companies offer airboat tours in the area, such as Wild Florida and Black Hammock Adventures.

Visit a local farm or ranch:

  • Learn about the agricultural heritage of Marion County and taste fresh produce at a farm like Appleton Farms or Whispering Pines Tree Farm.
  • Take a farm tour or participate in farm-to-table dining experiences.

Go stargazing:

  • Escape the city lights and enjoy the stunning night sky at one of the many dark sky observation sites, such as the Ocala National Forest.
Apply Now

Additional Resources

  • Ocala/Marion County Visitor & Convention Bureau: https://members.gainesvillechamber.com/list/member/ocala-marion-county-chamber-economic-partnership-1438
  • Tripadvisor: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Tourism-g34496-Ocala_Florida-Vacations.html
  • Visit Gainesville: https://www.visitgainesville.com/

This list offers only a glimpse of the many possibilities for enjoying your time in Marion County. Remember to consider your interests, budget, and desired pace when planning your activities.

Have fun exploring!

Close to the water and other attractions

Marion County, Florida is not directly on the coast, but it is strategically located with convenient access to both the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean. Here’s how:

Distance:

Gulf of Mexico: The closest point on the Gulf of Mexico is Crystal River, which is approximately 45 miles west of Ocala, the county seat of Marion County.

Atlantic Ocean: The closest point on the Atlantic Ocean is Daytona Beach, which is about 65 miles east of Ocala.

Accessibility:

Highways: Major highways like I-75 and Florida’s Turnpike connect Marion County to both coasts efficiently. The drive to each coast takes approximately 1-1.5 hours.

Benefits of Proximity:

  • Diverse Activities: Marion County residents can enjoy the best of both worlds: the calm waters and sandy beaches of the Gulf Coast and the vibrant atmosphere and thrilling water sports of the Atlantic Coast.
  • Economic Opportunities: The county’s proximity to both coasts fosters economic development in tourism, trade, and other sectors.
  • Balanced Climate: Marion County experiences a more moderate climate compared to the extremes on the coasts, offering a comfortable year-round living environment.

Overall:

While not directly on the coast, Marion County’s convenient location offers easy access to both the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean, allowing residents and visitors to enjoy the best of both coasts.

In Conclusion

Marion County, Florida, is more than just a location; it’s a vibrant community with a rich tapestry of experiences waiting to be explored. From its thriving job market with top employers like HCA Florida Hospitals and Lockheed Martin to its historical sites, cultural venues, and outdoor adventures, Marion County has something for everyone. Whether you’re a resident enjoying the balanced climate or a visitor reveling in the proximity to both the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean, this county offers a unique blend of opportunities and natural beauty. As you consider your interests, budget, and pace, remember that Marion County invites you to have fun exploring its many possibilities.

h1: Owning a Home in Sunshine State: Your Guide to Florida Property Tax Exemptions
body:
Congratulations on becoming a homeowner in the beautiful state of Florida! As you settle into your new abode, navigating the world of property taxes might seem daunting. But worry not, sunshine awaits in the form of property tax exemptions designed to lighten your financial load. Let’s delve into the most significant exemption – the homestead exemption – and explore other tax-saving opportunities available to Florida homeowners.

Homestead Exemption: Your Property Tax Shield

Imagine a $50,000 shield protecting your wallet from property taxes. That’s essentially what the homestead exemption does! This valuable benefit deducts $50,000 from your home’s assessed value, significantly reducing your taxable amount.

Here’s how it works:

  • Eligibility: To qualify, your property must be your primary residence on January 1st of the tax year. You must also own and occupy the home for at least seven months of the year.
  • Benefits: The exemption applies to all taxing authorities, including county, municipal, school district, and special taxing districts. This translates to lower property tax bills and savings that can be put towards other expenses or reinvested in your home.

Double Dipping with the Save Our Homes Cap

Florida’s Save Our Homes assessment limitation acts as a bonus layer of protection. It caps the annual increase in your home’s assessed value to 3% or the Consumer Price Index (CPI), whichever is lower. This prevents sudden spikes in your property tax bill due to rising market values.

Beyond Homestead: Exploring Other Exemptions

While the homestead exemption is the most common, Florida offers additional tax breaks for specific situations. Here are some noteworthy possibilities:

  • Senior Citizen Exemption: If you’re 65 or older and meet certain income requirements, you can qualify for an additional $50,000 exemption on your home’s assessed value.
  • Disabled Person Exemption: Permanently disabled residents and their spouses may be eligible for a $50,000 exemption, with additional exemptions for certain disabilities.
  • Veteran’s Exemption: Florida honors its veterans by offering a $50,000 exemption to certain disabled veterans and their surviving spouses.
  • Blind Person Exemption: Individuals who are legally blind in both eyes may qualify for a $50,000 exemption.

Claiming Your Exemptions: A Smooth Sail

The process for claiming exemptions is generally straightforward. Most counties allow online applications through their property appraiser’s websites. You’ll typically need to provide proof of eligibility, such as your driver’s license, Social Security number, and documentation supporting any additional exemptions you claim.

Remember: Apply for exemptions by March 1st of each year to ensure they’re reflected in the following year’s property tax bill.

Sailing Through Your Florida Property Tax Journey

By understanding and claiming the available exemptions, you can significantly reduce your property tax burden and enjoy the financial benefits of homeownership in Florida. Remember, knowledge is power – the more you know about these tax-saving opportunities, the smoother your financial sail will be on the Sunshine State’s property tax seas.

Bonus Tip: Don’t hesitate to reach out to your local property appraiser’s office for personalized guidance and assistance with claiming exemptions. They’re there to help you navigate the process and ensure you receive all the tax breaks you’re entitled to.

If you are purchasing a home in Florida contact a lender 

Taking Your Tax Savings with You: Portability in Florida’s Property Tax System

Picture this: you’ve built a comfortable life in your Florida homestead, enjoying the sunshine and watching your home’s value rise steadily. Thanks to the “Save Our Homes” (SOH) cap, your property tax hasn’t skyrocketed despite the appreciating market. But, life takes unexpected turns – you might want to downsize, move closer to family, or simply chase a new adventure. Does that mean leaving your tax-saving SOH cap behind? Thankfully, no! Enter portability, a unique feature of Florida’s property tax system that allows you to take your SOH benefit with you when you move to a new homestead within the state.

Here’s how it works:

  • What you transfer: Portability allows you to transfer the difference between your assessed value (property value for tax purposes) and your market value (actual market value) from your old homestead to your new one. This difference, often referred to as the “SOH assessment difference,” represents the tax savings you’ve accumulated thanks to the SOH cap.
  • What you can transfer: You can transfer the full SOH assessment difference up to a maximum of $500,000. If your new home has a higher market value than your old one, the entire difference applies. However, if your new home has a lower market value, you can only transfer a proportionate share of the SOH assessment difference.
  • When you can transfer: You have three years from the date you leave your old homestead to claim portability on your new one. Make sure to apply for both the homestead exemption and portability by March 1st of the year following your move.

Benefits of portability:

  • Reduces property tax bill: By applying the SOH assessment difference to your new home, you effectively lower its taxable value, leading to a smaller property tax bill. This can be a significant saving, especially in areas with rapidly rising property values.
  • Increases affordability: Portability offers flexibility for life changes without worrying about a sudden jump in property taxes. This can make downsizing or relocating within Florida more financially feasible.
  • Promotes housing market mobility: Portability encourages homeowners to move within the state without being penalized for their accrued SOH benefits. This helps maintain a healthy housing market with increased options for buyers and sellers.

Things to keep in mind:

  • Portability only applies to Florida homesteads. You cannot transfer your SOH assessment difference to a property outside the state.
  • There are specific eligibility requirements for both the homestead exemption and portability. Consult your local county property appraiser or the Florida Department of Revenue for detailed information.
  • The process of claiming portability can be complex. Seeking assistance from a tax professional or your county property appraiser’s office is recommended.

Portability is a valuable tool that allows Florida homeowners to enjoy the security of their accumulated SOH tax savings even when they move within the state. By understanding how it works and utilizing its benefits, you can navigate life changes while keeping your property taxes under control.

So, raise a glass of sunshine-infused beverage to your new Florida home and enjoy the financial peace of mind that comes with understanding and claiming your property tax exemptions!

h1: Rebuilding Hope: How the FHA 203(h) Mortgage Aids Disaster Victims in Purchasing a New Home
body:
In the aftermath of a disaster, recovery and rebuilding can seem daunting. However, there is a ray of hope for those who have lost their homes due to severe weather events or other catastrophes. The FHA 203(h) Mortgage Insurance for Disaster Victims Program is designed specifically to aid individuals in Presidentially-Declared Major Disaster Areas (PDMDA). This program supports disaster victims in purchasing a new principal residence, providing a pathway to recovery and stability.

Understanding the FHA 203(h) Mortgage

The FHA 203(h) mortgage is a special federal assistance program managed by the Federal Housing Administration. It offers significant benefits to help disaster victims make a new start in a new home without the financial burden that typically comes with purchasing a property.

Key Benefits Include:

  • 100% Financing: One of the most compelling features of the FHA 203(h) mortgage is that it requires no down payment. Victims can finance the entire purchase price of their new home, which removes a significant barrier to homeownership post-disaster.
  • Flexible Underwriting: Recognizing the unique circumstances faced by disaster victims, the FHA 203(h) program offers flexible underwriting. This means that even those whose financial situations have been disrupted by disaster have a better chance of qualifying for a mortgage.
  • Fee Reductions: Applicants benefit from reduced application fees and other concessions, making it easier and more affordable to secure financing.

Qualifications for the FHA 203(h) Mortgage

To be eligible for this program, applicants must meet certain criteria:

  • Principal Residence: The home purchased with the FHA 203(h) loan must be intended as the borrower’s principal residence.
  • Location of Previous Home: The borrower’s previous home must have been located in a PDMDA and must have been destroyed or severely damaged.
  • Timing: The application for mortgage insurance must be submitted within one year of the disaster declaration. Extensions may be available if announced by FEMA.

The Application Process

Applying for an FHA 203(h) loan involves several steps:

  1. Documentation of Loss: Borrowers must provide documentation proving their residence was in a disaster area and was damaged or destroyed.
  2. Lender Search: It’s crucial to work with a lender approved to offer FHA loans. Southern Home Loans can guide applicants through the specific requirements and paperwork.
  3. Credit and Income Review: Despite flexible underwriting standards, applicants will still undergo a credit check and income verification to ensure they can manage their new mortgage payments.

A Path Forward

The FHA 203(h) Mortgage for Disaster Victims is more than just a financial product—it’s a crucial support system for individuals and families eager to move past the tragedy and rebuild their lives. By removing some of the financial hurdles associated with purchasing a new home, the FHA 203(h) helps pave the way for recovery and a stable future.

For those affected by disaster, exploring the benefits of the FHA 203(h) program could be an important step towards reclaiming stability and comfort in a new home.

h1: Rent vs. Own: Why Buying a Home Now Could Be Your Gen Z/Millennial Power Move
body:
Hold up, before you swipe right on that trendy new apartment listing, let’s talk real estate. As a Gen Z/Millennial yourself, you might be skeptical about jumping into homeownership. Student loans, skyrocketing rents, and FOMO-inducing travel pics on Instagram can make buying a home seem like a distant dream. But hear me out: purchasing a home now could be the smartest financial move you make.

Building Wealth, Brick by Brick:

It’s true, rent feels endless. Each month’s payment vanishes, leaving you with nothing but a roof over your head (and maybe a killer Spotify playlist). But with a mortgage, you’re investing in yourself. Every payment goes towards equity, a fancy term for ownership. Over time, as your home value appreciates, so does your net worth. It’s like a magic savings account that grows with you. Imagine the future you: selling your home for a profit, using it as a springboard for further investments, or simply enjoying the financial security it brings.

Don’t Wait for the “Perfect” Market:

Newsflash: there’s no such thing as a perfect housing market. Sure, prices might fluctuate, but remember, rent does too. And waiting for a dip could mean missing out on current historically low interest rates. Plus, the longer you wait, the more you miss out on potential appreciation. Think of it like this: would you wait for the “perfect” stock price before investing? Probably not. So why do the same with real estate, one of the most stable investments out there?

Unlocking Your Homeownership Journey:

Okay, you’re intrigued. But what about the hurdles? The dreaded down payment, the complex loan process – it can all feel overwhelming. But fear not, young grasshopper! There are resources available to help you leap over those hurdles:

  • Down Payment Assistance Programs: Did you know there are government and community-based programs offering grants or reduced-interest loans to help with your down payment? These programs can significantly lower the barrier to entry, especially for first-time homebuyers.
  • Non-Occupant Cosigners: Don’t have enough individual income to qualify for a loan? No sweat! Enlisting a financially stable parent, relative, or friend as a non-occupant cosigner can boost your application’s strength. Just remember, cosigning is a serious commitment, so ensure clear communication and expectations are set beforehand.

Homeownership More Than Bricks and Mortar:

Let’s face it, beyond the financial benefits, homeownership offers a sense of stability and freedom that renting just can’t match. It’s your space to personalize, grow, and build memories. Imagine painting your walls your favorite color, having friends over for backyard BBQs, or finally adopting that furry friend you’ve been dreaming of – all without landlord restrictions.

But Wait, There’s More!

Owning a home can also:

  • Improve your credit score: Consistent on-time mortgage payments are a surefire way to boost your creditworthiness.
  • Offer tax benefits: Depending on your location and income, you might be eligible for mortgage interest and property tax deductions.
  • Provide stability for your future: No more worrying about rent increases or unexpected lease terminations.

Remember, homeownership isn’t a one-size-fits-all journey. Do your research, explore your options, and talk to a qualified realtor and mortgage lender. They can guide you through the process, answer your questions, and help you find a home that fits your budget and lifestyle.

Buying a home might seem daunting, but trust me, Gen Z/Millennial friend, it’s an investment in your future self. Take the leap, unlock the door to your own space, and start building wealth, brick by brick. Ready to learn more. Contact the Southern Home Team powered by Luminate Bank. They can guide you in the right direction and help get you closer to building wealth.

P.S. Still unsure? There are tons of online resources and communities dedicated to young homeownership. Do some research, ask questions, and empower yourself to make informed decisions! Remember, knowledge is power, and the power to own your future is within your reach.

h1: Comprehensive Home Loan Services in Crystal River, Citrus County, Florida
sections:
Home Loans in Crystal River

Founded in 2006, Southern Home Loans is dedicated to serving the Crystal River community with all their home loan needs. We offer any sort of home loan you need at affordable rates.

We’re part of the Crystal River and Citrus County community ourselves, that’s why we’ve done our best to provide the best home loan options at the lowest available interest rates. When it comes to finding a quality home loan, it always pays to stay local.

Our History

Southern Home Loans was established in 2006 to provide the most comprehensive home loan services to those who qualify. We began with a mission to make customer service the most important thing that we do.

Because we’re a direct lender, we’ve been able to streamline the loan process to make it a whole lot easier for all of our customers. We can have you pre-approved for the perfect home loan within an hour.

Whether you’re looking to purchase your first home, looking to refinance your existing loan, or simply consolidate your debt, we have the experts who can make everything easier for you!

Home Loans Made Simple

The home loan process is not always easy, and that’s why we’ve established services that take the stress out of it for you. We have mobile and online services that allow you to get your approval fast so that you can begin the process right away.

With our online services, you simply click on the loan in the drop-down menu that you’re interested in to learn more about it, then begin the approval process to get started. It’s that easy!

We’ll Get You Qualified for a Reverse Mortgage in Crystal River

Folks who are 55 or over may meet the requirements for a reverse mortgage, and we’re the most qualified to help you if you’re interested. A reverse mortgage will use the equity in your home to help you pay for expenses. With a reverse mortgage, the lender pays you, and you don’t have to pay the principal or interest so long as you’re still living in your home. The money can be received as a single lump-sum payment or paid in installments over time, and there are no restrictions on how you use the money.

Let Us Be Your Home Loan Heroes!

We’ve established a reputation that’s second-to-none in the industry, and we’re very proud of that fact. No matter what sort of home loan is needed, we’re the ones more people in Crystal River turn to.

Get in contact with us today or follow the simple online process and we’ll be happy to help get the process started for you.

h1: Comprehensive Home Loan Services in Gainesville, Florida
sections:
Home Loans in Gainesville

Since 2006, Southern Home Loans has dedicated itself to providing excellent, affordable home loans to the people of Gainesville. We’ll quickly get you approved with affordable rates.

Because we live and work in Gainesville, we’re dedicated to serving the local community. If you’re looking for a good home loan, you should look no further than your own backyard. Ask us about all the options available to you.

We’re Committed to the Gainesville Community

We’re in touch with the Gainesville community, and we’ve been working with families employed by the University of Florida, helping them to get the home loans they need, for more than a decade. Gainesville was hit hard by the 2009 real estate crash but is well on its way to a full recovery, and we’re helping that progress by providing the best loan rates possible.

hero.h1: Home Loan Services in Williston, Chiefland, Cedar Key, and Across Levy County, Florida
hero.lead: For nearly two decades, Southern Home Loans has helped families and individuals across North Central Florida find the right home loan, and Levy County is right next door to our Ocala office. About one in four Levy County residents is 65 or older, which is one reason we focus on loans that work for people on a fixed income, including reverse mortgages. Levy County is a place of small towns, open land, and Gulf Coast communities, and your home loan should fit the way you live here. Whether you’re buying acreage outside Williston, building near Chiefland, or settling into a home in Cedar Key, our loan specialists will find the option that fits your situation and your budget.

h1: Home Loan Services in Williston, Chiefland, Cedar Key, and Across Levy County, Florida
sections:
Home Loans in Levy County

Since 2006, Southern Home Loans has helped homebuyers and homeowners throughout North Central Florida. You’ll find options for nearly every need, from purchase loans and refinancing to lot and land loans, construction loans, and rural housing (RHS) loans.

Because we’re based just across the county line in Ocala, you get a lender who knows the area and is easy to reach. When you’re making one of the biggest financial decisions of your life, it pays to work with someone close to home.

Our History

Southern Home Loans opened in 2006 with one goal: put customer service first. That focus still guides everything we do.

As a direct lender, we’ve built a simpler, faster loan process for you. In many cases, you can be pre-approved within an hour.

Whether you’re buying your first home, refinancing your current loan, or consolidating debt, our team will walk you through each step and make the process easier.

Home Loans Made Simple

Getting a home loan doesn’t have to be stressful. With our online and mobile tools, you can start your approval from home and move forward quickly.

Choose the loan you’re interested in from the menu to learn more, then start your approval when you’re ready. Prefer to talk it through? Give us a call and a local specialist will help.

We’ll Help You Qualify for a Reverse Mortgage in Levy County

If you’re 55 or older, a reverse mortgage may help you use the equity in your home to cover everyday expenses, healthcare costs, home updates, or anything else you need. With a reverse mortgage, you receive payments instead of making them, and you don’t make principal or interest payments for as long as you live in your home. You can receive the money as a lump sum or in installments over time.

Your Local Home Loan Team

Levy County homeowners and homebuyers count on Southern Home Loans for clear answers, local service, and loan options that fit real life here. Whatever kind of home loan you need, we’re ready to help.

Contact us today or start the simple online process, and we’ll get things moving for you.

h1: Full Range of Competitive Mortgages and FHA Loans in Florida
sections:
Mortgages and FHA Loans

Florida home loans come in many forms, including conventional and FHA loans. We specialize in offering a wide range of mortgage options and can provide sound advice on which loan program is best for you and your family.

Florida Mortgage Loans

From fixed-rate mortgages to adjustable-rate mortgages, there is something for everyone in the Florida mortgage market. Florida also has a variety of government-sponsored loan programs such as FHA loans. These can provide qualified buyers with the loan they need at great rates.

Of course, with so many different types of mortgages in Florida, it’s important to get a deal that meets your financial needs and goals. That’s where our team comes in. We’ll look at your circumstances carefully and talk you through all the options.

Florida FHA Loans

FHA loans are insured by the Federal Housing Administration and offer many benefits that make them attractive to borrowers. For starters, they only require a minimum 3.5% down payment. They are also more forgiving of credit scores, making it easier for people with less-than-perfect credit to secure financing.

They can provide an excellent opportunity to get into the housing market in Florida with relative ease and at reasonable rates. FHA loans are available for both purchase and refinance.

If you’d like to know if you’re eligible for an FHA loan, just give us a call.

Florida Renovation Loans

Renovation loans, also known as home renovation loans, are a popular financing option if you’re looking to buy a property that needs repairs or renovations.

These loans are like a purchase and construction loan combined. They allow you to buy the home you want and the funds for renovation become available right after closing.

If you’re interested in a home renovation loan, give us a call to learn more.

Florida Construction Loans

Florida construction loans are a great solution for anyone looking to build in the Sunshine State. There are a variety of options available and the right one will provide you with a flexible repayment schedule and competitive interest rates.

Some loan companies offer construction loan packages that come bundled with additional services like architectural and engineering design guidance.

If you’re looking for an efficient way to finance a new building project in Florida, consider applying for a construction loan.

Mobile Home Loans in Florida

Mobile home loans are a great option if you’re looking to purchase a mobile home in Florida. These loans are available at affordable rates and they can be used to finance both new and pre-owned mobile homes.

With the right loan, you’ll be free to get the best possible deal on your new mobile home. The rate and terms on mobile home loans can vary so it’s important to get reliable professional advice before you sign on the dotted line.

If you’d like to know more about mobile home loans, contact our friendly team today.

Home Refinancing Loans in Florida

Home refinancing loans in Florida are an excellent way to capitalize on your investment. Refinancing your home can allow you to take advantage of lower interest rates, which will reduce your monthly payments.

Home refinancing loans in Florida are also ideal for homeowners who want to switch lenders or consolidate debt. If you’re considering refinancing your home, it’s important to get specialist mortgage advice before making any decisions.

Speak to our helpful team today to find out more about home refinancing.

Always Get Professional Mortgage Advice

Whether you’re interested in a mortgage, FHA loan, or refinancing, it’s vital to get professional advice from licensed mortgage specialists like Southern Home Loans. We can find exactly the right type of loan for your needs at rates you can afford.

Find Out if We Can Help You Refinance or Buy Your Next Home

Home Loans in Spring Hill

Southern Home Loans is a home loan and mortgage company that is dedicated to all things related to home loans and mortgages in Spring Hill, Florida. We’ll help you get started on building your dream home, provide the necessary loan to move into a house on the market, or provide a loan on your current home.

Spring Hill is growing extremely fast, as is indicated by census information. As more people flock to the area, we’re the local lender that they trust to give them the best loans with the most affordable rates.

Whether you’re new to the Spring Hill area or have lived here for years, we have all the loan tools you need. We can help you with the following home loan tools directly on our site:

Because we were established in 2006, we’ve watched as Spring Hill has grown dramatically over the last decade or so. As a direct lender that works with current and future homeowners, we’re proud of the fact that we’ve helped to contribute to the continued growth of the area.

As Spring Hill continues to grow and its residents look to us to provide them with financial solutions, we’re dedicated to making our customers happy by giving them the best experience they could ever ask for.

There’s a lot that goes into applying for a home loan, whether you’re looking to have a brand new home built or simply looking to take out a mortgage on your current property. Because we understand this, we’ve worked tirelessly to make things easier for you.

Our integrated online system is set up to do just about everything for you without giving you the runaround or sending you to any third party. We’re a direct lender, so all you have to do is provide your information and let us take care of the rest.

h1: Strategies to buy your Dream Home prior to selling your current home: 4 Strategies to Make it Happen
body:
The housing market is hot, and finding your dream home can feel like winning the lottery. But what if you haven’t sold your current place yet? Don’t worry, there are ways to snag that new house without the stress of temporary homelessness. Here are 4 strategies to buy before you sell:

1. Unlock Your Home’s Equity with a HELOC

A Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) lets you tap into the value you’ve built up in your current home. It’s like a credit card for your house, giving you access to funds for your down payment and closing costs. Here’s the catch: You’ll need good credit, a steady income, and enough equity in your home (typically over 20%). While HELOCs offer lower interest rates initially, they are variable and can fluctuate with the market.

Pros:

– Affordable and Simple: Often free to obtain with straightforward qualification.

– Access to Cash: Provides significant funds for your new home purchase.

– Interest-Only Payments: Manageable monthly payments.

Cons:

– Processing Time: Can take a while to secure.

– Qualification Impact: May affect your ability to qualify for a new mortgage.

2. Become a Cash Buyer with Our Power Buyer Program

We’ve crafted a solution that turns you into a cash buyer, enhancing the appeal of your offer and giving you a competitive edge. Our Power Buyer Program eliminates the common obstacles with traditional financing, such as mortgage contingencies and extended closing times. This gives you a major advantage in a competitive market – sellers love the speed and certainty of a cash offer. There is a program fee, and you’ll accrue some interest until you secure permanent financing for your new home.

Pros:

Competitive Edge: Cash offers are more attractive to sellers.

Simplified Process: Avoids the complications of traditional financing.

Faster Transactions: Allowing you to buy your new home before you sell your exiting home (in as little as 14 days).  

Cons:

Power Buyer Fee: There is a fee for the use of the funds and interest accrues until you close your long-term financing. 

3. Bridge Loan: A Temporary Boost to Buy Your New Home

Need a temporary funding solution? A bridge loan uses the equity in your current home to buy your new one. You won’t have to make immediate payments on the bridge loan, but you’ll need to sell your current home within a specific timeframe (usually around 6 months) to repay it. This option is good for short-term financing, but be aware of closing costs and fees associated with bridge loans.

Pros:

Substantial Funds: Access to significant cash for your new home.

No Immediate Payments: Easier to qualify for a new mortgage.

Quick Process: Close in as little as 14 days.

Cons:

Costs: Fees of 2.3-2.4% of the loan amount.

Equity Requirement: Must have a 25% equity cushion post-loan.

4. Rent Out Your Current Home and Become a Landlord

If you can handle the responsibility, renting out your current home can be a smart move. You’ll keep the benefits of your low mortgage rate and generate rental income that can help qualify you for a new mortgage. Renting comes with its own challenges, like finding good tenants and dealing with maintenance issues.

Pros:

Retain Low-Rate Mortgage: Keep the benefits of your existing low-rate mortgage.

Inflation Protection: Homes and rental income generally rise with inflation.

Additional Income Stream: Generate rental income.

Cons:

Landlord Responsibilities: Managing tenants and property upkeep.

Financial Risk: Vacancies can impact your finances.

Qualification Challenges: Future rental income may not fully offset your current mortgage payment.

The Takeaway

Buying a new home before selling your old one is a strategic decision. Each approach – HELOC, cash buyer program, bridge loan, or renting – has its pros and cons. Carefully consider your financial situation and goals to choose the best option for a smooth move into your new dream home.

Ready to Get Started?Contact us today to discuss your options and find the perfect strategy for buying your new home before selling your current one!

h1: Strengthen Your Offer with a TBD Full Underwrite Approval
body:
In today’s competitive real estate market, homebuyers are constantly seeking ways to make their offers more attractive to sellers. One way to do this is to obtain a TBD full underwrite approval from a mortgage lender. Most lenders require an executed contract from the buyer before they will underwrite the loan. A TBD underwrite approval is a conditional approval that indicates to the seller that the buyer’s financing is strong and that they are likely to be able to close on the property.

What is a TBD Full Underwrite Approval?

In a TBD full underwrite approval, the lender will go through the entire underwriting process, just as they would if the borrower had already found a home to buy. This means that they will verify the borrower’s income, assets, and employment information. They will also review the property appraisal and title report. Once the underwriter has reviewed all of this information, they will issue a conditional approval letter. This letter will state the maximum loan amount that the borrower is eligible for and the interest rate they will be offered.

Benefits of a TBD Full Underwrite Approval

There are several benefits to obtaining a TBD full underwrite approval before putting an offer in on a home. These benefits include:

  • Stronger negotiating position: A TBD full underwrite approval gives the seller confidence that the buyer’s financing is solid. This can make the buyer’s offer more attractive to the seller, especially in a competitive market.
  • Faster closing process: Once the buyer has found a home and the seller has accepted their offer, the closing process can move much faster if the buyer has already been fully underwritten. This is because the lender has already verified all of the borrower’s documentation and does not need to do any additional underwriting.
  • Reduced risk of the loan falling through: A TBD full underwrite approval can also reduce the risk of the loan falling through after the buyer has made an offer on a home. This is because the lender has already determined that the borrower meets all of their requirements.
  • Enhanced Peace of Mind: Knowing your financing is in place provides peace of mind and allows you to focus wholeheartedly on finding the right property without worrying about potential financing roadblocks.
  • 5. Negotiating Power: A TBD approval can strengthen your position when negotiating with the seller. You can potentially request concessions on price or closing terms, knowing your financing is already secured.

How to Get a TBD Full Underwrite Approval

To get a TBD full underwrite approval, you will need to contact Southern Home Loans with Luminate Bank and complete a mortgage application. The lender will then review your documentation and verify your information. Once the underwriter has reviewed your file, they will issue a conditional approval letter.

To qualify for a TBD full underwrite approval, you’ll typically need to provide extensive financial documentation, including:

  • Credit reports
  • Income verification documents
  • Asset verification documents (bank statements, investment accounts, etc.)
  • Employment verification

Conclusion

A TBD full underwrite approval can be a valuable tool for homebuyers who want to make their offers more attractive to sellers and ensure a smooth closing process. If you are considering buying a home, I encourage you to talk to Southern Home Loans at Luminate Bank about whether a TBD full underwrite approval is right for you.
